pitch: Research, connect, configure, verify, and launch Quip Bot without putting credentials into the AI conversation.
pitchMark: without putting credentials into the AI conversation
problem: A useful WordPress assistant needs grounded knowledge, approved wording, consent, escalation rules, and a testable launch decision.
Chat-based setup tempts people to paste WordPress passwords, provider keys, or license keys into the transcript.
This skill keeps human authorization in the browser, secrets in native credential stores, and only reviewed non-secret artifacts in the project.

flow.d: Confirm authority, compatibility, recovery, and off visibility.
Read public pages and collect only unresolved owner decisions.
Use human browser consent and the operating-system credential store.
Compile the closed configuration and show its exact SHA-256.
Write idempotently after approval, with snapshot and rollback.
Pass readiness, request separate go-live approval, then revoke access.

commands: Set up Quip Bot on my WordPress site
Research my site before configuring Quip Bot
Connect this site to my Quip Bot Pro account
Apply this approved Quip Bot configuration
Review whether Quip Bot is ready to go live

callout.label: Free core and Pro
callout.text: **Quip Bot core is free forever** and needs no quip.bot account. Pro is a separate $200/year entitlement; provider usage is billed separately.

items.name: Browser consent
items.desc: WordPress and optional Pro login stay human-operated in the system browser.

items.name: Native credential storage
items.desc: Uses macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager and prints redacted JSON.

items.name: Approved configuration
items.desc: Validates a closed schema, fingerprints it, applies idempotently, and snapshots rollback.

items.name: Write-only provider entry
items.desc: The human enters the provider key in a loopback-only local form.

items.name: Site-bound Pro
items.desc: Uses PKCE and a one-time grant; each connected website gets its own activation.

items.name: Linux automation
items.desc: Uses the human-operated wp-admin fallback until a native credential backend is approved.

limits.label: Safety boundaries
items: No password, Application Password, provider key, license key, or token in chat or artifacts.
No browser automation, SSH, XML-RPC, SQL, or internal Quip Bot admin routes.
No production write without recovery; no initial apply and go-live in one approval.
